executive_summary: T1.A renormalization introduces THREE blocking numerical safety issues: (1) log(0) from zero/tiny f_lin unchecked, (2) cumulative X_cur overflow from K sequential renormalizations, (3) T2.A incremental cell_lf requires exhaustive cells_by_margin_cat coverage not verified in spec. All three must be mitigated before implementation.

high_risk.title: Unguarded log(0) in geometric mean computation
high_risk.description: Spec line 39: std::log(std::fabs(f_lin[...])) — no guard for f_lin[k][j] <= 0 before log. Current code ensures new_f is checked for finiteness (line 440: 'if (!std::isfinite(new_f) || new_f > kLinearOverflowThreshold)'), so new_f > 0 always. HOWEVER: margin entry at 1.0, and f_old is always > 0 due to initialization + finiteness check. BUT std::fabs() in the renorm spec is redundant — it suggests defensive handling for negative values that should never occur. This redundancy masks a latent assumption.
high_risk.mechanism: If any upstream path (constraint violation, extreme solver oscillation, or numerical instability during margin update) produces f_lin[j] <= 0 or NaN, std::log(std::fabs(f_lin[j])) yields -inf (log 0) or NaN (log of negative). These propagate into log_sum → exp(−inf or NaN) → c_k = 0 or NaN → division X_cur[c] /= c_k produces inf or NaN.
high_risk.consequence: Silent corruption of calibration result; X_cur becomes inf/NaN; subsequent capacity step detects overflow and falls back to log-space, defeating T1.A's purpose.
high_risk.likelihood: LOW in normal operation (new_f protected by isfinite check). MEDIUM if solver oscillates or encounters numerical instability mid-sweep.

high_risk.title: Cumulative X_cur overflow from K sequential renormalizations
high_risk.description: Spec line 49: 'for (int c = 0; c < ct.M_cell; c++) X_cur[c] *= c_k;' — executed per margin. If K=20 and multiple margins trigger renorm (not rare on highly constrained problems), X_cur is multiplied by c_k1 * c_k2 * ... * c_kM where M ≤ K. Each c_k is checked individually: 'if (c_k < 1.0/kOverflowThreshold || c_k > kOverflowThreshold)' (line 45), meaning c_k ∈ [1/1e7, 1e7]. Worst case: all K=20 margins renormalize with c_k ≈ 1e7 → X_cur *= (1e7)^20 = 1e140 → overflow.
high_risk.mechanism: No guard on cumulative product ∏ c_k across margins in same sweep. Individual c_k bounds do not guarantee ∏ c_k stays finite.
high_risk.consequence: X_cur overflow → late-sweep X_cur values become inf → capacity step detects and trips to log-space. T1.A fails to keep solver in linear path.
high_risk.likelihood: MEDIUM on highly constrained, multi-margin problems. LOW on well-posed instances.

high_risk.title: T2.A incremental cell_lf assumes exhaustive cells_by_margin_cat coverage
high_risk.description: Spec lines 82–89 (T2.A): 'Maintain cell_lf[c] = Σ_k lf[k][g_k(c)] — updated when lf changes. When lf[k][j] changes by delta: cell_lf[c] += delta for c in bucket(k,j).' This assumes cells_by_margin_cat[k][j] lists ALL cells c affected by margin k category j. If cells_by_margin_cat[k][j] is sparse or omits cells, cell_lf is incomplete → X_tilde[c] = exp(log_X_init[c] + cell_lf[c]) is wrong.
high_risk.mechanism: Incomplete cells list → missing cell_lf updates → X_tilde underestimated → capacity step clamps to bounds prematurely, or margin satisfiability is false-negative.
high_risk.consequence: Silent calibration error; result violates input margin targets with no warning.
high_risk.likelihood: MEDIUM — depends on cells_by_margin_cat construction (likely inherited from cell_table compression). If cells_by_margin_cat is sparse or filtered (e.g., for cache efficiency), this is a real bug.

medium_risk.title: exp(log_sum / cnt) can overflow if log_sum is very large
medium_risk.description: Spec line 44: 'double c_k = std::exp(log_sum / cnt);'. If f_lin[k][j] ≈ 1e300 (large but valid), log(1e300) ≈ 691 → log_sum = 691 * cnt. Even with cnt=10, log_sum/cnt ≈ 69. exp(69) ≈ 6e29, well within double range. But if f_lin approaches 1e308 or a pathological case accumulates log_sum > 700, exp(log_sum/cnt) can overflow to inf.
medium_risk.mechanism: Large f_lin values (from oscillating target) → large log_sum → exp(log_sum/cnt) ≈ inf if log_sum/cnt > 709.
medium_risk.consequence: c_k becomes inf → X_cur[c] *= inf → overflow trip.
medium_risk.likelihood: LOW in practice (f_lin checked against 1e7 threshold). But possible if thresholds are loose.

medium_risk.title: T1.B assumes n_per_cell[c]=1 for all c when M_cell==st.n — no upstream validation
medium_risk.description: Spec lines 66–68: 'When M_cell == st.n (every obs is in its own cell), X_tilde[c] is identical to X_cur[c]'. This assumes n_per_cell[c] == 1. If a malformed input or bug in cell_table construction produces duplicate observations in same cell, this assumption breaks.
medium_risk.mechanism: Malformed input → n_per_cell[c] > 1 for some c when M_cell == st.n → X_tilde != X_cur → skip X_tilde produces wrong result.
medium_risk.consequence: Silent calibration error; result is infeasible.
medium_risk.likelihood: LOW — input validation should catch this upstream.

medium_risk.title: T2.B row-major rebuild: cost is O(K*M_cell) exp() calls, not O(M_cell)
medium_risk.description: Spec lines 91–101 say row-major rebuild is 'one sequential pass per margin', but the pseudocode shows nested loops: for each margin m, for each cell c, accumulate cell_lf[c]. Then rebuild X_tilde with O(M_cell) exp() calls. Spec claims '3-5x speedup vs current column-major', but doesn't account for K passes before the final exp loop.
medium_risk.mechanism: K sequential passes over M_cell + 1 pass of M_cell exp(). Total memory traffic: (K+1)*M_cell*8 bytes. Current column-major touches K*4MB arrays simultaneously (DRAM contention). Row-major touches 4MB per pass K times (prefetcher-friendly). So speedup is real, but not from eliminating exp() — from improving cache locality.
medium_risk.consequence: Spec is correct in intent but imprecise in cost model. Implementation should follow spec's row-major order.

mitigations_required.mitigation: Add guard in renormalization loop: 'if (f_lin[k+offset] <= kMinFactor || !std::isfinite(f_lin[k+offset])) skip this margin or clamp to kMinFactor.' Propose kMinFactor = 1e-300 (safe lower bound for finite log).
mitigations_required.verification: Log must show NO renormalization skipped on test benchmarks (indicates guards not firing); on contrived pathological inputs, guards catch before NaN propagates.

mitigations_required.mitigation: Track log-space cumulative renorm: log_cumul += log(c_k) per margin. Before multiplying X_cur by c_k, check: 'if (log_cumul > 700 || log_cumul < -700) trip overflow now'. Alternatively, cap c_k directly: 'c_k = std::clamp(c_k, 1.0/sqrt(kOverflowThreshold), sqrt(kOverflowThreshold))' to limit product.
mitigations_required.verification: Benchmark kk1204 K=20 must show renorm fires but overflow_trip never true after mitigation.

mitigations_required.mitigation: Mandate in spec: 'cells_by_margin_cat[k][j] must be exhaustive: for every cell c with g[k][c]==j, c must appear in cells_by_margin_cat[k][j]. Verify at log-path entry: for each margin k, sum |cells_by_margin_cat[k][j]| over all j must equal M_cell.' Add assertion in code.
mitigations_required.verification: On log-path entry, run exhaustiveness check; fail loudly if cells_by_margin_cat is incomplete.

mitigations_required.mitigation: Clamp log_sum before exp: 'double c_k = std::exp(std::clamp(log_sum / cnt, -700.0, 700.0));' — ensures exp result stays in [0, 1e304].
mitigations_required.verification: None needed; clamp is idempotent on normal log_sums.

mitigations_required.mitigation: Add assertion at line 66 (T1.B entry): 'if (M_cell == st.n) for (int c = 0; c < M_cell; c++) assert(n_per_cell[c] == 1);' Fail loudly if assumption breaks.
mitigations_required.verification: Test on well-formed inputs (should pass); on malformed inputs (should fail with assertion).

blockers: T1.A-1 and T1.A-2 must be resolved before code review. These are silent corruption paths with no upstream error detection.
T2.A-1 exhaustiveness must be documented and verified at runtime.
All mitigations must include test cases that exercise the guard conditions.
suggestions: Consider refactoring renormalization to use log-space cumulative product from the start, eliminating repeated multiplications of X_cur. This would be simpler than guards.
Add explicit test: pathological input where K=20 margins all renormalize with c_k ≈ 1e6 → verify no overflow.
T2.A: document the semantics of cells_by_margin_cat exhaustiveness in ieppa.cpp header comments, not just in spec.
questions: Is f_lin guaranteed to stay positive throughout all margin updates, or are there oscillating/damping phases where it could dip below 1e-300?
What is the actual expected range of c_k values on typical problems (e.g., kk1204, raking benchmarks)? This informs whether M2 guards will fire in practice.
Does cells_by_margin_cat currently support sparse indexing, or is it already exhaustive by construction in the cell_table module?
Can you provide a concrete test case (input data) that triggers multiple simultaneous renormalizations? Current spec examples don't show K > 1 renorms in same sweep.
For T1.B (M_cell == st.n), what is the actual frequency of this condition? If rare, the 8MB save may not justify the extra complexity.
